text: A delivery problem. A refund failure. An account warning. It looks familiar — and it wants you to act now.
Scammers imitate the brands and moments we trust. One rushed tap can expose passwords, payment details, or an account.
Before you tap, pause. The warning signs are often visible.
Look for urgency. Unknown senders. Domains that resemble a real service but do not belong to it. And familiar logos or confident wording designed to lower your guard.
Meet ScamShield: a mobile-first progressive web app that helps you assess a suspicious message or screenshot before you click.
Open ScamShield on your phone, choose a screenshot, and submit it for analysis. The flow is built for the moment that matters: when you are uncertain and need a clearer next step.
ScamShield uses A.I.-assisted analysis to examine what is visible in the image, including sender context, wording, links, and signs of impersonation.
In seconds, it returns a risk level, a plain-language explanation, the signals that influenced the assessment, and practical guidance for what to do next.
You see the risk at a glance, without having to decode every detail yourself.
You understand why the message looks suspicious, from sender mismatches to time pressure and payment requests.
And you get safer actions: do not tap the link, never share passwords or one-time codes, and verify through the official app or website.
ScamShield supports your judgment; it does not replace it. Low risk is never a guarantee.
Take a breath. Check the screenshot. Choose the safer next step. ScamShield — Check before you trust.
